models.title: Diffusion index from externally classified component directions
models.summary: The diffusion index averages direction codes rather than the magnitudes of component growth.

relationship.original_equation: Diffusion index=(sum of1,0.5,0 component scores / number of components)*100 in published display
relationship.locator: Learning Module4, Economic Indicators / Diffusion Indexes, printed p239 (PDF p251), unnumbered four-component example
relationship.translation_notes: Uses the previously covered arithmetic-mean operator on an independently defined economic breadth quantity. This is explicitly a derived index definition with classified-score inputs; it neither duplicates raw observations nor claims to estimate GDP. Base100 display scaling is external; count is a dimensionless integer supplied by len.

variables.definition: Preclassified direction scores for the chosen index components and horizon:1 positive contribution,.5 essentially unchanged,0 negative; threshold/direction transformations external
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship
variables.domain: 1-256 values each exactly0,.5or1; endpoint and indicator-sign rules explicitly set upstream

variables.definition: Mean classified directional breadth normalized to[0,1]
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: component direction codes follow a consistent horizon and positive-contribution sign convention.
Source assumption: near-zero thresholds and inversions such as declining unemployment claims are resolved before binding.
limitations: Individual score membership cannot be enforced with the scalar guards; external binding must check the discrete set.
No conditional classification or threshold boundary is implemented; this is not a raw-growth arithmetic mean.

models.title: Income velocity of a specified money stock
models.summary: Income velocity divides nominal output by a specified money stock; the quantity equation is the equivalent accounting identity.

relationship.locator: Learning Module4, Inflation and Velocity, printed p257 (PDF p269), unnumbered definition; Learning Module5, Quantity Theory, printed p287 (PDF p299), Equation(2)
relationship.translation_notes: The financial period is a dimensionless convention fixed in context; no seconds conversion is made. The quotient cancels currency dimensions. M*V=P*Y follows by nominalGDP=P*realGDP from the deflator record and is not independently counted as another equation.

variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Income turnover count of the selected stock per declared financial output period
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: money aggregate, GDP coverage, average/observation date and income period are explicitly selected.
Source assumption: GDP is nominal, not reference-price realGDP.
limitations: Velocity need not be stable and is not a causal money-to-inflation forecast.
A broad money stock is not interchangeable with the monetary base; annualized quarterly GDP affects the turnover period.

models.title: Observed nominal-minus-inflation-linked yield spread
models.summary: The reading compares nominal and inflation-protected yields to obtain an inflation-compensation proxy and cautions that other market factors affect it.

relationship.original_equation: Implied inflation compensation=nominal bond yield - inflation-protected bond yield
relationship.locator: Learning Module4, Inflation Expectations, printed p258 (PDF p270), unnumbered10-year bond-yield example and caveat
relationship.translation_notes: Both yields are decimal fractions on a shared annual convention; subtraction returns a decimal yield spread. No positive-only guard is imposed because observed compensation can be negative.

variables.definition: Annual nominal government-bond yield on the chosen maturity, pricing and compounding convention
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Real quoted yield of the comparable inflation-linked government bond, same maturity and yield convention
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Observed inflation-compensation yield difference, which is not pure expected inflation
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Source assumption: matched currency, issuer credit, maturity and yield/compounding conventions.
Source assumption: quoted inflation-linkage terms, lags and deflation protections are specified externally.
limitations: The spread includes inflation-risk and relative-liquidity effects and therefore cannot be labeled a pure inflation expectation.
The simple yield difference is a market spread convention; it is not the exact one-period Fisher conversion already covered by engineering-finance--fisher-real-rate.
